title: Gaia astrometric support for 14 timing-variable binaries persists after six-factor matching but depends on two detections
abstract: We test Gaia support for 14 timing-variable binaries in a published TESS screen. We retrieve Gaia DR3 records and reproduce the combined astrometric count of 2 of 14 against 1 of 393 quiet binaries. The quiet detection is variability-induced motion, not acceleration. The acceleration-only count is 2 against 0. Matching all 407 systems on magnitude, parallax, color, two scan measures and eclipse period gives a conditional combined-indicator probability of 0.00741, against 0.00324 without adjustment. Magnitude-parallax grids give 0.00223-0.00353. Smaller six-factor matched samples give 0.00659-0.0741. A bounded hidden factor of 2.96 in within-set timing-group assignment odds can raise the full-match probability to 0.05. Removal of either positive case removes nominal significance in each fixed-ratio match. Thus measured selection factors do not remove the association, but two detections do not establish an intrinsic triple rate. Limits include inherited timing rules, uncertain source matches, unmeasured Gaia selection and exploratory tests. We include retrieval code, exact tests, an independent enumeration check and input hashes. External record-level data stay outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Conditional astrometric association tests and hidden-bias limits for the fixed set of 14 timing-variable and 393 quiet binaries. Tests share observations. They do not give independent replications or a full Gaia selection correction.

citations.reason: We use its timing classes and test its population astrometric association with matched controls. We distinguish its combined astrometric outcome from acceleration alone.
Gaia DR3 astrometric binary processing and selection; Halbwachs et al. 2023.
